channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Nvidia board launches independent investigation after Jensen Huang admits affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation on Sunday after CEO Jensen Huang told staff he had a romantic relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence believes was recruited by China. The board says it has no reason to believe company secrets were compromised — but the inquiry puts the AI chipmaker under a new kind of scrutiny.

item.title: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx: the best AI agent finishes just 12% of real professional work
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: SemiAnalysis dropped frontier AI models into simulated workplaces — deal rooms, live trading desks, real CAD software — and gave them eight hours per task. The best model in the world finished 12% of the work. Finance and legal scored zero.

item.title: Claude Code plays PC games in the background: the open-source MCP that drives GTA without touching your mouse
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A developer built an MCP server that lets Claude Code play Windows games in the background — injecting input and capturing frames inside the game process, so the game never needs focus and your mouse stays yours. The video shows it driving in GTA IV and V, making story choices in Detroit: Become Human, and finishing one game start to finish.

item.title: Clone a voice on your own machine: a hands-on guide to IndexTTS 2.5
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: IndexTTS 2.5 clones a voice from a single short clip — zero-shot, locally, in five languages, with emotion and speed control. This guide installs it, clones a voice in the WebUI and the Python API, and checks what it can and can’t do.

item.title: Microsoft's ThinkingBox: two in three failed AI agent runs looked finished
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Microsoft's expanded ThinkingBox evaluation graded 121,680 AI agent trials by the database state they left behind — and found 67.24% of failed runs still looked complete. The same check also trains: 50 steps of reinforcement learning nearly tripled a small open model's repeatable successes.

item.title: Opus 5.5 built an infinite, self-evolving Backrooms — and Reddit is arguing over whether it feels like the Backrooms at all
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A Reddit creator gave Claude Opus 5.5 one standing order — keep building this world — and the result is a browser game that grows new yellow rooms on its own. The 100-second tour passed 800 upvotes overnight, and then the top comment asked the awkward question: is it actually the Backrooms?

item.title: Differentiable computer vision, batched: hands-on with Kornia 0.9
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Kornia 0.9 turns PyTorch tensors into a complete computer vision toolkit: batched transforms with per-sample parameters, annotated augmentation, SIFT matching, and homography estimation — all differentiable, all on CPU. This guide installs 0.9.0 and verifies every step.

item.title: Run AWS on your laptop for free: hands-on with Floci, the LocalStack replacement
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: LocalStack’s free edition is gone — auth tokens, frozen updates. Floci is the MIT-licensed replacement: 128 AWS services on localhost:4566, no account, no token. This guide installs it three ways, runs a five-service pipeline against it, and shows where it stops being AWS.

item.title: Hands-on with Meta's Astryx: the design system built for coding agents
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Meta’s Astryx is the design system that grew inside Meta for eight years — 174 components, seven themes, and a CLI that writes the component guide into your agent’s instructions. This guide installs 0.7.11, builds a working app, wires the CLI into your coding agent, scaffolds a full analytics dashboard, and themes it — every step verified.

item.title: DeepMind VP says AI science is hitting a phase transition, with new releases coming in weeks
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Pushmeet Kohli says DeepMind is witnessing “a genuine phase transition in the pace of scientific discovery”, with a glimpse coming in releases over the next few weeks. Here is what he actually said — and what he did not.

item.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 adds GIFs, saved reference images, and two faster API models
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.6 on November 4: prompts and photos can now become looping GIFs, reference images of people, pets, and characters can be saved and reused, and two new API models — Flare and Sunburst — generate images 50% faster. Users now create more than 4 billion images a week.

item.title: Turn any document into an AI classroom: hands-on with OpenMAIC
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenMAIC turns a topic or a PDF into a full interactive classroom — AI teachers, classmates, a whiteboard, and quizzes — running on your own machine. This guide installs it with Docker, wires up a model, and generates your first lesson.

item.title: Two agents, one repo: run Claude Code and Codex together with OpenAI’s official plugin
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI’s Codex plugin puts a second frontier coding agent inside Claude Code — reviews, rescues, and session handoffs without leaving your chat. This guide installs it, proves every command, and shows the three workflows that actually earn their keep.

item.title: RoboSpoof: doctored video made frontier AI robots attempt unsafe tasks 97% of the time
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Robocurve put five frontier models in charge of a pair of robot arms and fed them three versions of the same scene. With clear footage they refused unsafe tasks most of the time; blur the camera and the refusals collapsed — doctored footage pushed attempts to 97%.

item.title: Turn any website into a design system you can reuse: hands-on with designlang
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: designlang points a real browser at any live website and reads the design system off the DOM — DTCG tokens, a Tailwind theme, Figma variables, a graded report card. This guide extracts Stripe’s design, applies it to a project, grades two sites head to head, and wires the MCP server into an agent — every step verified.

item.title: Observer turns your phone into a local AI watchdog — and Reddit is asking whether it needs an LLM at all
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A video of Observer, an open-source agent that watches whatever your phone’s camera sees and pings you on WhatsApp when something moves, topped r/LocalLLaMA on Saturday. The thread likes the idea — and immediately asked why a language model is doing a job plain computer vision could do faster.

item.title: Apple quietly ships an official Xcode plugin for Claude Code — no announcement, just a merged PR
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Apple is now listed as the author of an official Xcode plugin in Claude Code's marketplace, giving the agent build, test, preview, and simulator control — and the company hasn't said a word about it.

item.title: Canva cuts 1,271 jobs in its first mass layoff as AI costs bite and growth stalls
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Canva is cutting or relocating 1,271 roles — about 22% of its workforce — after growth slowed for the first time in a decade. AI is at the centre of the story, but not in the way the headlines suggest: it is the cost and the competitor, not the replacement.

item.title: RUMOR: Qwen-4-Flash-Early tops a community game-making benchmark, narrowly beating Claude Opus 5.5
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: An early, unreleased Qwen checkpoint leads a small community leaderboard that asks models to build playable 2D games. The margin is thin, the test is narrow, and Alibaba has confirmed nothing — here’s what the numbers actually say.

item.title: Hex local voice dictation: hold a key, speak, and it pastes
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Hex is free, open-source voice dictation that runs entirely on your machine — hold a key, speak, let go, and your words paste into any app. This guide installs it, runs a first dictation, swaps speech models, and drives it from the terminal.

item.title: OpenAI pledges to pay its own data-centre power bills in a National Community Compact
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Two days after midterm voters backed curbs on data-centre expansion, OpenAI published a National Community Compact promising to cover the full cost of its campuses' electricity, publish site-level water and power figures, and stop asking local officials to sign NDAs. The catch: the promises are voluntary, and OpenAI grades its own homework.

item.title: Charts your coding agent can actually draw: hands-on with Microsoft Flint 1.0
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Your coding agent can write a chart spec, but the chart it draws is usually wrong — wrong type, unreadable labels, no interaction. Microsoft’s Flint 1.0 is a visualization language built for agents: one semantic spec compiles to five backends, with 14 themes and 23 interaction presets — this guide wires in its MCP server, renders a first chart, and compiles the same spec three ways, every step verified.

item.title: Theo, a wheeled humanoid robot, restocked a Zurich supermarket on camera — and Reddit is checking the 400-items-an-hour claim
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A video of Theo, a wheeled humanoid robot, restocking shelves in a Zurich supermarket spread fast on r/singularity: 400 items an hour, overnight, in the dark. The top comments did the math — and the poster conceded the number comes with conditions.

item.title: Meta buys Conductor, the multi-agent coding startup — and its cloud service shuts down November 20
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Meta has acquired Conductor, the startup that lets developers run several AI coding agents in parallel workspaces. The team joins Meta Superintelligence Labs — and Conductor Cloud goes read-only on November 13, then shuts down on November 20, with user data deletion to follow.

item.title: Reverse-engineer any video with rea-video: tell filmed, AI, and code apart, shot by shot
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: JuneYaooo/rea-video (3,681 stars on November 7, 2026, Apache-2.0) reverse-engineers any video shot by shot — filmed, AI-generated, 3D, or built in code — and hands you a remake plan: what to film, what to generate, what to code. It runs in Claude Code or Codex, needs only ffmpeg and Python 3.10+, and its offline tools-only mode is free. Hands-on: the install, your first breakdown, reading the report, and planning the remake.
